sections.h2: Which Brevard Clerk office can I walk into to record a document?
sections.html:
The Clerk of Court and Comptroller runs six public offices spread along the county, and any of them can direct you to the Recording Division. The Clerk serves as county recorder, so deeds, mortgages and liens all land in one general series of Official Records books.

sections.h2: Can I trust the online Official Records Search in Brevard?
sections.html:
Use it to find documents, and treat the printouts as unofficial. The Clerk's own notice says the online records are not official, that only the records held at its branch offices count as the Official Public Records, and that checking accuracy is up to the searcher.

  • Try every spelling variation of a name, since the index matches what was typed at recording.
  • No password or fee is needed to search.
  • Restricted information requires a User Subscription Form for Official Records View, and a renewal fee keeps that subscription active.
  • Copies of recorded documents come only from the Clerk's office.

One warning matters for sellers. Federal tax lien entries on the site are not identical in content to what the IRS filed, so the Clerk says searches cannot be relied on in proceedings about title, sales or foreclosure involving a federal lien. Call (321) 637-2004 for the filed copy.

sections.h2: What does the Brevard Clerk actually record?
sections.html:
The Clerk's list of recordable instruments includes deeds, mortgages, liens, contracts, affidavits, subdivision plats, surveys, condominium declarations, bills of sale, judgments, certificates of military discharge and declarations of domicile. Recording happens on payment of statutory fees, and most of the traffic involves real estate. The Recording Division presents its online search as a public service, separate from the books themselves.

That breadth explains why a title search turns up more than ownership. A Brevard parcel can show a recorded judgment against a prior owner or a condominium declaration that governs the building, and both can affect a sale.

sections.h2: How do I get private details removed from the Brevard records site?
sections.html:
Two Florida laws from 2021 give people a written path. A request under Chapter 2021-215 asks the Clerk to remove information exempt under sections 119.071 and 119.0714, or an image of a military discharge, a death certificate, or certain family, juvenile or probate matters. It must be notarized, state the statutory basis and confirm you qualify for the exemption.

Names in the Official Records index stay unless the name itself contains a street address, as a trust or company name might. Send removal requests to P.O. Box 2767, Titusville, FL 32781-2767, by fax at (321) 264-5246, by email to fs119exemptionrequest@brevardclerk.us, or at a branch. A separate Chapter 2021-231 notice lets an affected person ask the Clerk to add the identity of a respondent in certain minor-protection injunctions, using the case number and the acclaimuseradmin@brevardclerk.us address.

sections.h2: What does the Brevard Property Appraiser add to a records search?
sections.html:
The Brevard County Property Appraiser site, BCPAO.us, says no appointment is needed for in-person help and carries market data pages on median single-family sale prices, median market value by property type and the gap between market and assessed value. It also holds real property value history and a sales percentage breakdown by property type.

The homepage also advertises an Amendment 3 information link about major homestead exemption changes, and a banner announcing the homestead filing deadline. Read it before listing, since exemption rules decide what a buyer inherits.

sections.h2: What fees and stamp tax come with a Brevard deed?
sections.html:
State statute 28.24 sets the clerk's recording schedule per page, with small extras for added names and for trust fund and technology charges, so a longer deed costs more than a short one. Ask the Recording Division for a quote on page count before you mail anything.

Deed stamp tax under statute 201.02 is levied on consideration, which includes any mortgage the buyer takes over. All signers share liability, and the Clerk collects it when the deed is recorded. Estate planning deeds get no special break, while a deed from a personal representative handling a probated estate is on the state's not-taxable list.

sections.h2: What should a Brevard seller gather before recording?
sections.html:
• A deed signed before two witnesses, as Florida land conveyance law requires.
  • The parcel number and legal description matching the last recorded deed.
  • Payoff letters for any mortgage or lien your search turned up.
  • The stamp tax figure and a check for the recording total, or an arrangement through the title company.
  • Proof of homestead status, if any, to share with the buyer, since a sale resets the assessed value.

sections.h2: How should I plan around the Brevard branch map?
sections.html:
The offices run from Titusville in the north through Merritt Island and Viera to Melbourne and Palm Bay in the south, so pick the one nearest your title company or home. Titusville has two sites, South Street and the Parkway Complex, and Palm Bay and Merritt Island close over the midday stretch, so a lunchtime trip to either can fail.

The Property Appraiser, a separate elected office, posts its own holiday and early closure calendar on BCPAO.us, with some branch closings listed by date. Check it before driving over for an exemption question, because a Clerk visit and an appraiser visit follow different schedules.

sections.h2: How do I work through a Brevard title search step by step?
sections.html:
• Start with the current owner's name and the parcel number from the appraiser's site.
  • Search the Official Records under each spelling or married and maiden name, then repeat for earlier owners back to a clear chain of deeds.
  • Note every mortgage, lien, judgment and declaration, and which have a recorded release.
  • Order certified copies from the Clerk for anything you must rely on, because online images are unofficial.
  • Raise a federal tax lien with the Official Records Department, since the web index may differ from what the IRS filed.

Finishing this before listing means any unreleased mortgage from an earlier owner surfaces while there is still time to ask the lender for a satisfaction. The Clerk records whatever is presented, so a missing release will not announce itself; only the search reveals it. Keep a list of each document number you reviewed, because the title company will ask for the same references.

faqs.q: Where does Brevard County record deeds?
faqs.a: With the Clerk of Court and Comptroller, acting as county recorder, at any branch office. The Official Records Department number is (321) 637-2004.

faqs.q: Is the Brevard online records search official?
faqs.a: No. The Clerk says only the records at its branch offices are the Official Public Records, and searchers should try all spelling variations of a name.

faqs.q: Can personal identifiers be taken off Brevard's records website?
faqs.a: Yes, for information the law makes exempt. Send a notarized written request that states the statutory basis, by mail, fax or email to the Clerk.

faqs.q: Does the Clerk's name index drop my name on request?
faqs.a: Not usually. Party names stay in the index unless the name itself contains a street address.

faqs.q: Does a Brevard deed owe documentary stamp tax?
faqs.a: Generally yes. The tax is based on consideration and every party to the document is liable. The state's list of exceptions includes a deed signed by an estate's personal representative.
